sources.entry: django-wiki - Wiki system with complex functionality for simple integration and a superb interface. Store your knowledge with style: Use django models. (Demo) GPL-3.0 Python

summary.one_liner: django-wiki is a pluggable wiki application for Django projects that stores content and revisions in Django models and renders Markdown.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes django-wiki as a wiki system built as a reusable Django app, installable from PyPI under the package name "wiki". It stores wiki content in Django models and uses Markdown as its markup language, with the renderer built into the core. The project says it is designed around a plugin API, with features meant to be added through plugins rather than the core. Hierarchical pages with per-page permissions are mentioned, and the README says the project supports multiple wikis in the sense of nested hierarchies with their own permissions. Customization is described as done through template overrides, template tags, Bootstrap SCSS theming, and plugins. Revision history is handled internally rather than through django-reversion, according to the Q&A section.
use_cases: host an internal knowledge base inside a Django site
add a wiki with Markdown pages to a Django project
maintain collaborative documentation with page permissions
extend a wiki through a plugin system
store wiki content in a relational database via Django models
how_to_run: Follow the installation and setup instructions in the docs/ folder (not reproduced in the README)
A Docker container is mentioned in the README (Docker tl;dr section); no command is given in the README text
notable: Plugin API intended as the main extension point, keeping optional features out of the core
Content and revisions stored as Django models rather than in markup text
Hierarchical page trees with permissions at each level
Fully translated into 13 languages via Transifex, per the README
Published on PyPI as 'wiki' and provides a Docker container
caveats: Requires a Django project; it is a Django app, not a standalone server, and the README expects users to know Django for customization
The README says the project is 'always a work in progress', and the plugin and model APIs may still change in smaller ways
Supported Django versions are listed per release; older Django versions are dropped in newer releases
